title: Restaurant Menu
story: You're designing a digital menu for a cafe. Each item has a name, price, and size (Small, Medium, Large). You need to format the price nicely — "$4.50" instead of just `4.5`.
why: Combining enums and structs models real products where choices (like size) affect the final item.
analogy: A menu item is like a configurable product online — you pick the product (name), see the base price, then choose a size option from a fixed list.
try_it: Add an `IceBlended` variant to the Size enum (it costs 2x the base price). Add a `category` enum with Coffee, Tea, Food variants and attach it to MenuItem. Create a breakfast menu with 4 items.
tips: Use `if item.size == Size.Large` to compare enum values — simple equality check
When creating a modified copy, list all fields explicitly — it makes the transformation clear
Float64 values display as numbers; concatenate with strings to format them as text
common_mistakes: Comparing `item.size == "Large"` instead of `item.size == Size.Large` — Size is not a string
Forgetting to copy unchanged fields when creating a modified MenuItem (name stays the same)
